tools.name: environment_variable_set
tools.description:
Set one of an Environment's variables (the one id names): every command on its Workspaces' Containers, their Setup and Start Scripts and the Environment's Build get it. The same rules as the user's Edit dialog: at most 50 variables, values of at most 4096 characters, and names a shell can export, other than those the Container sets itself (PATH, HOME, GITHUB_TOKEN, CLOUDPID_…).

With id "*" the variable is kept Global, for a value that is shared and not secret (an email, a URL); an Environment's own variable of the same name wins, and the 50 counts an Environment's own and the ones it inherits together, so a call that would leave any Environment with more is refused. Each Environment's Build is made with it, so a new Build is asked for in each Environment that does not override it.

Variables are plain: every command, and you, can read them, and they are not taken out of output. Never put a credential in one: a value holding a Secret this Session holds, or a GitHub token, is refused, and so is a Secret Reference, which is not resolved here.

The change is recorded with your reason, and the user can see and revert it on the Environments page. It applies at each Workspace's next Container start; for this Session's own Environment, container_restart applies it now.

tools.name: environment_container_resize
tools.description:
Set the Container size of an Environment (the one id names): the size the next Container of every one of its Workspaces starts on, and the size they keep after each idle stop.

Sizes, by memory, then vCPU:
- lite: 1/16 vCPU, 256 MiB memory, 2 GB disk
- basic: 1/4 vCPU, 1 GiB memory, 4 GB disk
- cpu-1: 1 vCPU, 3 GiB memory, 12 GB disk
- standard-1: 1/2 vCPU, 4 GiB memory, 8 GB disk
- mem-4: 1 vCPU, 4 GiB memory, 12 GB disk
- standard-2: 1 vCPU, 6 GiB memory, 12 GB disk
- cpu-2: 2 vCPU, 6 GiB memory, 12 GB disk
- mem-8: 1 vCPU, 8 GiB memory, 12 GB disk
- standard-3: 2 vCPU, 8 GiB memory, 16 GB disk
- cpu-3: 3 vCPU, 9 GiB memory, 12 GB disk
- mem-12: 2 vCPU, 12 GiB memory, 12 GB disk
- standard-4: 4 vCPU, 12 GiB memory, 20 GB disk

Memory is what a running Container costs, so a larger size costs more for every Workspace of the Environment. The Environment's size limit bounds the size: a larger one is refused, and the limit is a Limit that only the user can raise, with environment_container_size_limit_set, which asks for their Approval.

This changes the Environment, not a Container that runs: it keeps the size it started on, and a size container_resize gave it holds there until its idle stop. To restart only this Workspace's current Container at another size, for more memory now, use container_resize, which changes no Environment.

With id "*" the setting is changed at Global: every Environment that does not override it inherits it, and a new Build is asked for in each whose Build is made with it. Setting an Environment's value makes it the Environment's own (an Override), which a later change at Global does not reach; environment_setting_reset makes it inherit Global's again. The change is recorded with your reason, and the user can see and revert it on the Environments page. It applies at each Workspace's next Container start; for this Session's own Environment, container_restart applies it now.

tools.description:

On (the default), the Environment keeps one Workspace made ahead from its last good Build while it had a Session in the last 3 days: cloned, its Setup Scripts run, its Container snapshotted and stopped, so a new Session takes it and starts without waiting for the clones and the Setup Scripts. tools.name: environment_skill_save
tools.description:
Save a Skill for an Environment (the one id names), from its folder in the Workspace: a folder you wrote (such as /workspace/.cloudpid/tmp/<name>), or one `npx skills add <source> --copy` made. Every Workspace of the Environment then serves it read-only at /workspace/.agents/skills/<name>, over the Skill of the same name kept Global, and lists it among the skills; Workspaces of other Environments do not. A Skill of the same name the Environment keeps is replaced. Saving a Skill whose name is also kept Global makes the Environment's own copy, which wins in this Environment only.

With id "*" the Skill is kept Global: each Environment's Workspaces serve it at their next readying (this Session's at once, unless its Environment keeps its own Skill of the name). A Skill there steers every future Session, so the user must approve the change, reading the Skill on the card: it shows the first 16000 characters of the files and warns the user of what it cuts, so keep a Skill at Global small enough to review in full, or expect it to be declined. The user is asked for their Approval on a card in the Session (and a notification): the call waits for the answer, with no deadline. On Approve the change is made and recorded as approved; on Decline nothing changes, and the result carries their reason. If the Skill of the name was saved again, or the folder's files changed, meanwhile, the approval does not apply and you are told to ask again.

The folder holds a SKILL.md whose YAML frontmatter sets name (1 to 64 lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, not starting or ending with a hyphen, no two in a row, and the folder's own name) and description (at most 1024 characters, saying what the Skill does and when to use it), and any files it refers to. tools.description:
Install Skills from GitHub for an Environment (the one id names): fetched by cloudpid, not by you (no Container, no `npx skills`), pinned to the commit the source's ref resolves to, and kept with their Skill source (repo, path, ref, commit). Every Workspace of the Environment then serves each at /workspace/.agents/skills/<name>, read-only; a Skill of the same name the Environment keeps is replaced.

source is owner/repo, owner/repo@skill, or a GitHub URL such as https://github.com/owner/repo/tree/<ref>/<path> (the first segment after tree/ is the ref, so write a branch name with a slash as feature%2Ffoo; without one, the default branch is used). Public repos work, and so do private ones in an account the GitHub App is installed on. Other sources (GitLab, other hosts, well-known indexes) are not fetched here: run `npx skills add <source> --copy` in a Container and save the folder with environment_skill_save.

With id "*" the Skills are kept Global: each Environment's Workspaces serve them at their next readying (this Session's at once, unless its Environment keeps its own Skill of the name). Set the Subagent Workspace limit: how many Subagent Workspaces (subagent with workspace "new": a Workspace of its own, with its own Container) one Session may have at once, default 1. Each runs a Container of its own, which costs while it runs. It is a Limit, so the user must approve the change, at either Scope. Subagent Workspaces that exist stay.

Give scope "*" to change Global, which each Environment inherits unless it overrides the field, or an Environment's id (environment_list shows them) to override Global for that Environment's Sessions only; there is no default. At an Environment the value is kept as its Override even when it equals Global's, so the field stops following Global until settings_reset removes the Override.

The user is asked for their Approval on a card in the Session (and a notification): the call waits for the answer, with no deadline. On Approve the change is made and recorded as approved; on Decline nothing changes, and the result carries their reason. If the user changes the same setting meanwhile, the approval does not apply and you are told to ask again.

The change is recorded with your reason, and the user can see and revert it on the Settings page. Each Session runs with its own Environment's Settings (its Overrides over Global over the defaults): a change at an Environment reaches only that Environment's Sessions, and a change at Global only those whose Environment does not override the field. A Session it reaches uses it from its next request (this one) or when it next admits input (the others); the result says whether it reaches this Session.

tools.name: settings_reset
tools.description:
Reset one setting at a Scope: with an Environment's id, remove the Environment's Override of the field, so it inherits Global again; with scope "*", put the field back to its default at Global (an Environment that overrides it keeps its Override). A field the Environment does not override, or that is at its default at Global, changes nothing. The fields: model, thinkingLevel, roles.small, roles.medium, roles.large, roles.xlarge, compaction.enabled, compaction.reserveTokens, compaction.keepRecentTokens, compaction.backgroundTokens, tools.offered, spendLimit.perSession, branchSummary.skipPrompt, mcp.servers.<name>, mcp.servers.<name>.enabled, mcp.servers.<name>.exposure, mcp.servers.<name>.toolExposure, extensions.<extension>.<key>. A Role is one field (its model and hint together), and so is each extension option.

Resetting a Limit (spendLimit.perSession, extensions.subagents.maxSubagentDepth, extensions.subagents.maxSubagentWorkspaces) waits for the user's Approval at either Scope, as the Limit tools do: The user is asked for their Approval on a card in the Session (and a notification): the call waits for the answer, with no deadline. On Approve the change is made and recorded as approved; on Decline nothing changes, and the result carries their reason. If the user changes the same setting meanwhile, the approval does not apply and you are told to ask again. Any other field is reset at once. An MCP server's field (mcp.servers.<name>.enabled, .exposure or .toolExposure) is reset only at an Environment, and only where it is an adjustment of a server Global or a Repo defines (settings_mcp_list shows the fields it holds); it is refused at "*", for a key of the Environment's own entry (use settings_mcp_disable or the exposure tools) and for mcp.servers.<name> itself (settings_mcp_remove removes a server). A reset that would make a switched-off server or a hidden tool reachable again waits for the user's Approval, as settings_mcp_enable does.

The change is recorded with your reason, and the user can see and revert it on the Settings page. Each Session runs with its own Environment's Settings (its Overrides over Global over the defaults): a change at an Environment reaches only that Environment's Sessions, and a change at Global only those whose Environment does not override the field. A Session it reaches uses it from its next request (this one) or when it next admits input (the others); the result says whether it reaches this Session.

tools.name: settings_instructions_set
tools.description:
Set the user's Instructions at one Scope: Markdown that conversations' models (each Session's root and its subagents) are shown in their system prompt from the start of their Context Window, before the Project instructions of the AGENTS.md files. They are what the user wants of every Session (Global) or of every Session in one Environment; what only one repo needs belongs in its Project instructions (AGENTS.md). Give the whole text: it replaces that Scope's Instructions, and an empty text removes them. At most 64 KiB of UTF-8 per Scope. settings_get shows them.

They steer conversations unasked, so the user must approve each change; set them only when the user asks. An approved change applies from each conversation's next Context Window (a new Session, a Handoff or a Rollover), never inside one: a context that has begun, this one included, keeps showing the Instructions it started with.

Give scope "*" for the Global Instructions, which every Session's conversations are shown, or an Environment's id for its own, which its Sessions' conversations are shown after the Global ones. They add up rather than one replacing the other: where two disagree the nearer wins, the Environment's over the Global ones, and the Project instructions over both.

The user is asked for their Approval on a card in the Session (and a notification): the call waits for the answer, with no deadline. On Approve the change is made and recorded as approved; on Decline nothing changes, and the result carries their reason. If the user changes the same setting meanwhile, the approval does not apply and you are told to ask again.

The change is recorded with your reason, and the user can see it as a line diff and revert it on the Settings page.
